name: Auto Producer
description: The generators that earn while you watch, and the cost curve that decides how long you watch. Each tier produces a resource on an interval and is bought at a price that grows geometrically, which is the shape that makes an incremental game feel like an incremental game: the next one is always nearly affordable. Tiers may produce other tiers rather than currency, and that is what turns a list of buttons into a machine. Production is computed from elapsed time rather than ticked per frame, so a slow frame does not cost the player output and a fast one does not gift it.

inputs.name: tiers
inputs.description: Generator definitions: id, base cost, cost growth, base output, and what the output is. Required — the tier ladder is the game.

inputs.name: costGrowth
inputs.description: Default multiplier applied to a tier's price per purchase. 1.15 is the genre's load-bearing constant.

inputs.name: bulkBuyEnabled
inputs.description: Whether x10 and max-affordable purchases are offered.

inputs.name: tickSeconds
inputs.description: Production interval. Output is elapsed-time based, so this is a reporting cadence rather than a rate.

outputs.name: nextCostByTier
outputs.description: Price of the next purchase per tier.
